headline: Medicare Drug Plan Premiums Are About to Jump for 25 Million Seniors
summary: Medicare beneficiaries may face higher premiums next year for their Part D drug plans, as the federal government plans to end subsidies that helped mitigate price increases in the program.  The Trump administration will not continue the subsidies beyond 2026, The Wall Street Journal reported.  About 25 million Medicare recipients are enrolled in a stand-alone Part D plan for their drug coverage.
